source_content.content: Figure[1](#S3.F1 "Figure 1 ‣ RLVR and PPO. ‣ 3.1 Preliminaries ‣ 3 Prefix-Based Rollout Reuse with Intermediate Step Rewards ‣ PRAISE: Prefix-Based Rollout Reuse in Agentic Search Training") provides an overview of PRAISE. The presentation of this section follows the same workflow: we first introduce the main search trajectory and prefix-state formulation, then describe prefix-based rollout reuse, and finally present reward construction and joint PPO optimization. ### 3.1 Preliminaries #### Task setup. Let $\mathcal{D}\={(q_{i},y_{i})}_{i\=1}^{N}$ denote a training set of query–answer pairs, where $q_{i}$ is a user query and $y_{i}$ is its ground-truth answer. For simplicity, we omit the sample index $i$ and write $(q,y)\sim\mathcal{D}$. The goal of agentic search is to learn a policy that, given a query $q$, interacts with an external search environment over multiple turns and finally produces an answer that matches $y$. #### Agentic search trajectory. We consider a multi-turn search setting with $T$ search turns. At turn $t\in{1,\dots,T}$, the model generates a reasoning segment $c_{t}$ and a search action $a_{t}$, and then receives an observation $o_{t}$ from the environment. After the final turn, it produces a final reasoning segment $c_{T+1}$ and outputs the answer $\hat{y}$. The resulting trajectory is | | $\tau\=\bigl(q,{(c_{t},a_{t},o_{t})}_{t\=1}^{T},c_{T+1},\hat{y}\bigr),$ | | (1) | | --- | --- | --- | --- | where $c_{t}$, $a_{t}$, $o_{t}$, and $\hat{y}$ correspond to , , , and , respectively, and $c_{T+1}$ is the final reasoning segment before answering. To expose the compositional structure of the trajectory, we define the prefix state as | | $s_{t}\=\begin{cases}\bigl(q,{(c_{t^{\prime}},a_{t^{\prime}},o_{t^{\prime}})}_{t^{\prime}\=1}^{t}\bigr),\&t\=1,\dots,T,\\[3.0pt] q,\&t\=0,\end{cases}$ | | (2) | | --- | --- | --- | --- | where $s_{t}$ denotes the information state after turn $t$, and $s_{0}$ contains only the original query and no external search interaction. Thus, ${s_{t}}_{t\=0}^{T}$ forms an ordered set of prefixes, where each $s_{t}$ contains exactly the information available after the first $t$ search turns. This corresponds to the Main Search Rollout part in Figure[1](#S3.F1 "Figure 1 ‣ RLVR and PPO. ‣ 3.1 Preliminaries ‣ 3 Prefix-Based Rollout Reuse with Intermediate Step Rewards ‣ PRAISE: Prefix-Based Rollout Reuse in Agentic Search Training"). #### RLVR and PPO. We train the agent under the RLVR setting, where reward signals are computed automatically from the generated answer and the ground-truth answer. Let $\pi_{\theta}$ denote the policy model with parameters $\theta$. At a high level, RL training aims to maximize the expected training utility of trajectories: | | $\mathcal{J}(\theta)\=\mathbb{E}_{(q,y)\sim\mathcal{D},\,\tau\sim\pi_{\theta}^{\text{search}}(\cdot\mid q)}\left[\mathcal{R}(\tau)\right],$ | | (3) | | --- | --- | --- | --- | where $\pi_{\theta}^{\text{search}}$ is the policy under the search prompt, and $\mathcal{R}(\tau)$ denotes the reward signal of the main search trajectory. In PRAISE, this signal is instantiated using the outcome reward together with intermediate process rewards, as detailed in the following subsections. In practice, we optimize this objective with PPO. *Figure 1: Overview of PRAISE. Left: Main Search Rollout. The policy performs multi-turn search and produces a complete trajectory with a final answer. Middle: Prefix Answering. PRAISE extracts prefix states and generates an intermediate answer from each prefix. Right: Reward Assignment and Joint optimization. Prefix answers are scored against the ground-truth answer, step rewards are computed from adjacent score differences, and the final answer receives a terminal reward. All resulting samples are jointly used for PPO training.* ### 3.2 Prefix-Based Answer Generation and Rollout Reuse #### Search mode and answer mode. The same underlying model $\pi_{\theta}$ is used in two modes with different prompts: | | $\displaystyle\pi_{\theta}^{\text{search}}(\cdot\mid q)$ | $\displaystyle:\=\pi_{\theta}(\cdot\mid P^{\text{search}}(q)),$ | | (4) | | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | | | $\displaystyle\pi_{\theta}^{\text{ans}}(\cdot\mid s_{t})$ | $\displaystyle:\=\pi_{\theta}(\cdot\mid P^{\text{ans}}(s_{t})),$ | | (5) | | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | where $P^{\text{search}}(\cdot)$ is the prompt template for multi-turn search, and $P^{\text{ans}}(\cdot)$ is the prompt template for generating an answer from a given prefix state. For each query $q$, the model first generates a full search trajectory | | $\tau\sim\pi_{\theta}^{\text{search}}(\cdot\mid q),$ | | (6) | | --- | --- | --- | --- | where $\tau$ is defined in Eq. ([1](#S3.E1 "In Agentic search trajectory. ‣ 3.1 Preliminaries ‣ 3 Prefix-Based Rollout Reuse with Intermediate Step Rewards ‣ PRAISE: Prefix-Based Rollout Reuse in Agentic Search Training")). We then extract the ordered prefix states ${s_{t}}_{t\=0}^{T}$ from $\tau$. For each prefix state $s_{t}$, the model generates a prefix answer | | $\tilde{y}_{t}\sim\pi_{\theta}^{\text{ans}}(\cdot\mid s_{t}),\qquad t\=0,1,\dots,T,$ | | (7) | | --- | --- | --- | --- | where $\tilde{y}_{t}$ is generated using only the information contained in $s_{t}$. In this way, PRAISE converts one full search rollout into multiple additional prefix-based answer-generation samples. Notably, prefix-based answer generation is only used during training; at inference time, the model performs only the main search rollout, so PRAISE introduces no additional inference-time cost. #### Rollout reuse. Each expensive search rollout $\tau$ is converted into multiple additional answer-generation samples, | | $\left{(s_{t},\tilde{y}_{t})\right}_{t\=0}^{T},$ | | (8) | | --- | --- | --- | --- | so that a single rollout yields $T+1$ prefix-based training samples rather than only one final-answer instance. These reused samples directly increase the amount of supervision obtained from each rollout, especially for long-horizon trajectories with many search turns. This corresponds to the Prefix Answering part in Figure[1](#S3.F1 "Figure 1 ‣ RLVR and PPO. ‣ 3.1 Preliminaries ‣ 3 Prefix-Based Rollout Reuse with Intermediate Step Rewards ‣ PRAISE: Prefix-Based Rollout Reuse in Agentic Search Training"). ([10](#S3.E10 "In Answer scoring. ‣ 3.3 Intermediate Step Rewards and Joint Optimization ‣ 3 Prefix-Based Rollout Reuse with Intermediate Step Rewards ‣ PRAISE: Prefix-Based Rollout Reuse in Agentic Search Training")); // 4. Process and outcome rewards for *$t\=1$ to $T$* do Compute the process reward $r_{t}^{\text{proc}}$ according to Eq. ([12](#S3.E12 "In Outcome reward for the main rollout. ‣ 3.3 Intermediate Step Rewards and Joint Optimization ‣ 3 Prefix-Based Rollout Reuse with Intermediate Step Rewards ‣ PRAISE: Prefix-Based Rollout Reuse in Agentic Search Training")); // 5. Reward assignment for the main rollout Construct token-level immediate rewards ${\rho_{k}}$ for the main rollout according to Eq. ([13](#S3.E13 "In Reward assignment. ‣ 3.3 Intermediate Step Rewards and Joint Optimization ‣ 3 Prefix-Based Rollout Reuse with Intermediate Step Rewards ‣ PRAISE: Prefix-Based Rollout Reuse in Agentic Search Training")); Append the main search rollout $\tau$ together with its token-level rewards ${\rho_{k}}$ to $\mathcal{B}$; // 6. Reused prefix samples for *$t\=0$ to $T$* do Set the terminal reward of the reused prefix sample according to Eq. ([14](#S3.E14 "In Reward assignment. ‣ 3.3 Intermediate Step Rewards and Joint Optimization ‣ 3 Prefix-Based Rollout Reuse with Intermediate Step Rewards ‣ PRAISE: Prefix-Based Rollout Reuse in Agentic Search Training")); Append the prefix-answer trajectory $(s_{t},\tilde{y}_{t})$ with terminal reward $r_{t}^{\text{ans}}$ to $\mathcal{B}$; // 7. PPO update Compute returns and advantages from $\mathcal{B}$, then update $\pi_{\theta}$ and $V_{\phi}$ using Eq. ([15](#S3.E15 "In Joint optimization with PPO. ‣ 3.3 Intermediate Step Rewards and Joint Optimization ‣ 3 Prefix-Based Rollout Reuse with Intermediate Step Rewards ‣ PRAISE: Prefix-Based Rollout Reuse in Agentic Search Training")) and Eq. ([16](#S3.E16 "In Joint optimization with PPO. ‣ 3.3 Intermediate Step Rewards and Joint Optimization ‣ 3 Prefix-Based Rollout Reuse with Intermediate Step Rewards ‣ PRAISE: Prefix-Based Rollout Reuse in Agentic Search Training")); *Algorithm 1 PRAISE Training within PPO* ### 3.3 Intermediate Step Rewards and Joint Optimization #### Answer scoring. Let $R(\cdot,\cdot)$ denote a verifiable answer scoring function that compares a predicted answer with the ground-truth answer. For each prefix answer $\tilde{y}_{t}$, we compute its *prefix score* | | $v_{t}\=R(\tilde{y}_{t},y),\qquad t\=0,1,\dots,T.$ | | (9) | | --- | --- | --- | --- | where $v_{t}$ is the score of the prefix answer $\tilde{y}_{t}$. We also compute the score of the final answer in the main search rollout: | | $u\=R(\hat{y},y).$ | | (10) | | --- | --- | --- | --- | where $u$ is the score of the final answer $\hat{y}$ from the main search rollout. #### Adjacent prefix gains as process rewards. We quantify the contribution of each search turn by measuring the change in answer quality from prefix $s_{t-1}$ to prefix $s_{t}$. Accordingly, the process reward at turn $t$ is defined as | | $r_{t}^{\text{proc}}\=\alpha\bigl(v_{t}-v_{t-1}\bigr),\qquad t\=1,\dots,T,$ | | (11) | | --- | --- | --- | --- | where $\alpha\geq 0$ is a scaling coefficient controlling the strength of process rewards. In this way, sparse terminal supervision is transformed into step-aligned feedback over the search trajectory. #### Outcome reward for the main rollout. In addition to the process rewards, the original search trajectory still receives a standard outcome reward based on its final answer: | | $r^{\text{out}}\=u$ | | (12) | | --- | --- | --- | --- | #### Reward assignment. For the main search rollout, PRAISE uses both the outcome reward and the process rewards. For each search turn $t$, let $m_{t}$ denote the index of the last token of the corresponding search segment, i.e., the end of the model-generated text that leads to the $t$-th search interaction, and let $m_{\text{ans}}$ denote the index of the last token of the final answer segment. We then define the token-level reward at position $k$ as | | $\rho_{k}\=\begin{cases}r_{t}^{\text{proc}},\&k\=m_{t}\text{ for some }t\in{1,\dots,T},\\[4.0pt] r^{\text{out}},\&k\=m_{\text{ans}},\\[4.0pt] 0,\&\text{otherwise}.\end{cases}$ | | (13) | | --- | --- | --- | --- | Under PPO return computation, these sparse token-level rewards propagate backward through the corresponding segments and provide credit signals to the search decisions that produced them. Meanwhile, each reused prefix-answer sample $(s_{t},\tilde{y}_{t})$ is treated as an auxiliary answer-generation trajectory with terminal reward | | $r_{t}^{\text{ans}}\=v_{t},\qquad t\=0,1,\dots,T.$ | | (14) | | --- | --- | --- | --- | Therefore, a single main search rollout provides two complementary forms of supervision: search-policy supervision on the original trajectory $\tau$, induced by the token-level rewards in Eq. ([13](#S3.E13 "In Reward assignment. ‣ 3.3 Intermediate Step Rewards and Joint Optimization ‣ 3 Prefix-Based Rollout Reuse with Intermediate Step Rewards ‣ PRAISE: Prefix-Based Rollout Reuse in Agentic Search Training")), and answer-generation supervision on the reused prefix samples, induced by the terminal rewards ${r_{t}^{\text{ans}}}_{t\=0}^{T}$. #### Joint optimization with PPO. We optimize the shared actor $\pi_{\theta}$ and critic $V_{\phi}$ using PPO over both the main search trajectory and the reused prefix-answer trajectories. Let $h_{k}$ denote the decoder context before generating token $x_{k}$, and let $\theta_{\mathrm{old}}$ denote the behavior policy used to collect the current batch. For each token position $k$, we compute an advantage estimate $\hat{A}_{k}$ and a return target $\hat{G}_{k}$, and define the importance ratio as inline formula $r_{k}(\theta)\=\frac{\pi_{\theta}(x_{k}\mid h_{k})}{\pi_{\theta_{\mathrm{old}}}(x_{k}\mid h_{k})}$. The actor is updated with the clipped PPO objective: | | $\begin{split}\mathcal{L}_{\mathrm{actor}}(\theta)\=-\mathbb{E}_{k}\Big[\min!\big(r_{k}(\theta)\hat{A}_{k},\;{}\\ \mathrm{clip}!\left(r_{k}(\theta),\,1-\epsilon,\,1+\epsilon\right)\hat{A}_{k}\big)\Big]\end{split}$ | | (15) | | --- | --- | --- | --- | where $\epsilon$ is the clipping coefficient. The critic is trained by regressing the return targets with a mean-squared-error loss: | | $\mathcal{L}_{\mathrm{critic}}(\phi)\=\mathbb{E}_{k}\left[\left(V_{\phi}(h_{k})-\hat{G}_{k}\right)^{2}\right].$ | | (16) | | --- | --- | --- | --- | Since both trajectory types are optimized with the same parameters $\theta$, PPO jointly improves search behavior and prefix-based answer generation within a unified training process. This corresponds to the Reward Assignment and Joint Optimization part in Figure[1](#S3.F1 "Figure 1 ‣ RLVR and PPO. ‣ 3.1 Preliminaries ‣ 3 Prefix-Based Rollout Reuse with Intermediate Step Rewards ‣ PRAISE: Prefix-Based Rollout Reuse in Agentic Search Training"). *Table 1: Main results on five QA benchmarks.
